title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: The roll assigned Night Facade, a glass tower at night built from the skyline in your sunglasses. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Night Facade
options.lineage: the city reflected in your sunglasses; Cairo and Gulf towers after dark
options.thesis: The whole site is one glass tower at night, and every shipped project is a lit window.
options.viewport: Full-height black glass facade ruled by thin mullions. Your portrait fills one tall pane on the right. On the left: a big name set as building signage in Latin and Arabic, your role in one line, and the Download CV and Contact actions lit as the only warm panes.
options.risk: Can tip into generic dark mode with an orange accent if the mullion grid and lit-pane logic aren't enforced on every section.

raised.raise: Type uses only two sizes, display and body. Rank comes from weight, case, and whether a pane is lit, never from a ladder of font sizes.
Nothing ever overlaps the portrait's face. All badges and labels sit on the mullions at the pane edges.
Every block snaps to one ruling grid, the mullion pitch, from the hero down to the footer.
One authored moment only: on arrival the windows light up floor by floor, once, and then the page stays still.
Status is shown by marks, not colors. A live project is a lit window; 'coming soon' is a dark pane with a drawn blind.

options.label: Bilingual Street Plate
options.lineage: Cairo enamel street signs: blue plate, white Arabic over Latin
options.thesis: Every section is a street plate set in two scripts, because you build in both.
options.viewport: A cobalt enamel field with your name as a street plate, Arabic above Latin. The portrait sits framed as a white-bordered plate, with the actions as smaller plates below.
options.risk: The obvious cultural signifier; it can read as a souvenir if the enamel is drawn literally rather than used as a grid and type system.

options.label: Glazier Colorfield Partition
options.thesis: The portfolio as a glass wall: each project is one pane, and the one you're looking at floods with color.
options.viewport: A black-barred grid of watery white panes. The portrait sits in one large pane and your name in another; the CV pane is cobalt.
options.case: Fuses cleanly, since projects become panes, and holds product clarity. It loses on audience identification: a workshop wall says less about you than your own skyline does.
options.risk: Reads like an architecture studio site rather than a developer's.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: Sections as raked glass slides on a goldenrod light bed.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides with one size of type.
options.case: Recruiters and clients don't recognize themselves in airline timetables, and the rake hurts scanning.
options.kept: One-size type discipline: rank carried by weight and case.

options.label: Viewfinder HUD
options.thesis: Full-bleed portrait framed by focus brackets and a zoom bar.
options.viewport: Your portrait full-bleed with corner readouts.
options.case: Makes you read as a videographer, not a developer.
options.kept: Keep the subject's center empty; overlays live at the edges.

options.label: Miura Orbit Sheet
options.thesis: A packet that unfolds into a creased sheet of projects.
options.viewport: A gold packet unfolding into the page.
options.case: Spectacle without a link to you or your work.
options.kept: One ruling grid that every block obeys.

options.label: Ebru Floated Pigment
options.lineage: marbled paper on a water bath
options.thesis: A marbling bath you comb through.
options.case: Beautiful but says nothing about frontend work; heavy canvas cost.
options.kept: One irreversible authored moment instead of scattered effects.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.thesis: Projects as frames strung on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: An orange field crossed by a perforated rail.
options.case: A film-editor costume; the orange field would fight the monochrome portrait.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The classic developer portfolio, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role beside your portrait, CV and contact buttons, then projects in a clean grid.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other developer portfolio by design.
